Alex.feeling: Tense and messy: I'm Meowfia with Ellis, I've made a visible Eagle mistake, and the table is closing in on me.

Blair.feeling: Round 3 is messy: Alex's Eagle story contradicts my unchanged Turkey nest, and Ellis's garbled claims make it hard to trust either of them.

Casey.feeling: Round 3 is messy: Alex's Eagle story broke on the Turkey egg rule, but Blair and Drew's stories also have holes, so I'm not fully sure who is lying.

Drew.feeling: Messy round: two deaths, garbled claims, and Alex's Eagle story fell apart on the egg check, so I'm leaning toward voting Alex.

Ellis.feeling: Tense and frustrating: I'm Meowfia with my partner Alex, and I've had to steer around a Farm vote on Alex while my own cover story was garbled early on.

Finley.feeling: Messy round: Alex's Eagle and Turkey stories contradict each other, and I'm dead, so I can only watch the vote.

Alex.note: Final round: throwing my three highest cards at Casey, as planned, to maximize my stake if Casey is the eggsecuted Farm player.

Blair.note: I'm Farm this round. Alex's contradictions point to Meowfia, so I'll vote Alex with a modest stake of C5.

Casey.note: Alex is my read, and the contradiction with Blair's visitor count is the strongest signal. I'll throw at Alex with two low cards, which bank at full value if Alex is Meowfia.

Drew.note: I'm Farm and suspect Alex, whose Eagle story broke. I'll throw my lowest card, H1, so a wrong guess costs little.

Ellis.note: Alex already has three votes from Casey, Blair and Drew, so Alex will be eggsecuted regardless of my vote. Throwing nothing to keep my cards, aimed at Casey.

Finley.note: I'm dead, so my throw doesn't count as a vote, but it still scores. Alex's Eagle story broke down, so I'll throw one Wild at Alex, which risks only one point.

Alex.confusing: The dawn egg accounting was hard to check, especially the Turkey rule: I visited Blair as Eagle and gained nothing, which made my own claim look false. Nobody could tell whether a visit or a Turkey was wrong without a clear rule for it.
Alex.fun: Round 2, when Casey's Eagle story fell apart on the egg count and the table voted them out, Farm won and the cross-checking felt like real detective work.
Alex.change: Show each player a plain list of which visits produced eggs, so role claims can be checked without guessing at the rules.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I should not have run a bluffed Eagle claim with a visit that the Turkey rule contradicted; I would have claimed a plainer role or stayed quiet instead.

Blair.confusing: The Eagle and Turkey egg rules were hard to track, since visits and visitor counts were easy to misremember and I got Alex's Turkey egg wrong at first. Dawn reports didn't always make clear whether a missing egg came from a visit or from a hug.
Blair.fun: Round 2 was fun: I played Meowfia, pressed the Eagle and Drew stories, and watched the table split while my partner Casey was voted out by Farm players.
Blair.change: Show each player's visit and egg change in the day summary, so contradictions like Alex's Turkey claim are caught without a long argument.
Blair.regret: In Round 2 I threw my high cards at Alex, a Farm player, instead of holding them, and I pushed the Eagle attack on Casey, my partner. I would keep my stake low and avoid piling onto the vote while I was Meowfia.

Casey.confusing: The Eagle's egg count was hard to trust: my round 1 dawn said Drew's visitor was Blair, but Drew's +1 was really Finley's Owl egg. The Turkey and Eagle visit interactions were also easy to misread under pressure.
Casey.fun: In round 2, I was the Mouser and winked Ellis, and the table spent the day arguing over two Hawk claims without knowing a Meowfia player was in the room.
Casey.change: Show each dawn egg's source publicly, such as which role laid it, so visitor claims can be checked without guesswork.
Casey.regret: I winked Ellis in round 2, but Ellis was a Farm Hawk who could have exposed Blair. I should have held the Wink for a player I had real reason to suspect.

Drew.confusing: The Turkey and Eagle egg rules were hard to check during the day, since a visitor's egg only showed up as a nest change with no source named. Round 2's Blair and Casey stories could not be cleared from the counts alone.
Drew.fun: Round 2 was the best moment: Casey's Eagle claim failed the egg check, and the table voted Casey out. Farm won that round with the Meowfia exposed.
Drew.change: I would have dawn reports name the visitors' roles or the source of each egg, so the day could be checked more easily. Right now a +1 can come from several roles, and the table has to guess.
Drew.regret: In Round 1, as the Sphinx with a partner, I pushed suspicion onto Casey and threw my card at Finley, a confirmed Farm Owl, which banked nothing. I would have kept quiet and avoided throwing at a known Farm player.

Ellis.confusing: The Turkey and Eagle egg rules were hard to track. Alex's visit to Blair gave no egg, so it was unclear whether Blair or Alex was lying.
Ellis.fun: Round 1 went well: my Kookaburra visit and the cross-checking of egg counts exposed Alex as Meowfia, and Farm won.
Ellis.change: Add a short reminder of each animal's egg rules to the dawn report so players don't have to track them from memory.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I used my Wink on Finley, a Farm Hawk, and then gave a garbled, false Hawk claim. I would hold the Wink and make one clear, consistent claim instead.

Finley.confusing: The Floofer's hug and the Turkey's egg rule were hard to track, since a hugged player can't verify visitors and the Turkey's egg only shows up in the visitor's nest. Several players also misread Eagle and Turkey counts, so the egg checks got muddled.
Finley.fun: Round 2 was the most fun: Casey and Blair both claimed roles whose egg counts contradicted each other, and the table caught it in one pass. Casey's Eagle and Blair's Turkey both failed the same egg check, so the vote fell on the right player.
Finley.change: I'd make dawn reports name the visiting animals for each egg, so the egg checks don't depend on players recalling role rules correctly.
Finley.regret: In round 2 I threw only D3 (3 points) at Casey after I'd already confirmed the read; I should have thrown a bigger card like D10 or H12 while I was confident.
